exposure: registration method (counting usual sleeping spaces vs. number of household members)
outcome: proportion of households having received a net from the campaign
proportion of households with one net for every two people
ownership of at least one ITN
cohort: The study included 13,901 households from 14 mass insecticide-treated net (ITN) distribution campaigns in five African countries.
finding: Successful household registration, influenced by factors like larger household size and presence of children under five, was the most important determinant of a household receiving ITNs, and universal coverage campaigns using a sleeping space allocation strategy were more effective in increasing the proportion of households with enough ITNs.
country: Ghana, Nigeria, Senegal, South Sudan, Uganda
cross-section timing: Three to 16 months after ITN distribution
